complaint: Email sends looked really slow starting the morning of March 9th. Someone said it was probably the sender deploy that day. Never confirmed.

response.restated_complaint: The engineer wants to know why email sends were slow starting the morning of March 9th, and whether the comms-sender deploy that day (c52a0f9) is responsible.

hypotheses.summary: 6 email sends between 2026-03-09T09:00:00.755Z and 2026-03-10T09:00:00.755Z took 4120ms vs a 235ms baseline (17.5x slower), all hitting provider 429s with 18 retries before eventually succeeding (final status 202) — this is the 'slow' behaviour the complaint describes. The suspected cause, comms-sender deploy c52a0f9 (PR #99, 'Add SMS provider seam', deployed 2026-03-09T14:00:00.000Z), is explicitly ruled out: it postdates the onset of slowness by 5 hours, and 3 of the 6 affected messages had already occurred before that deploy happened.
hypotheses.why_this_rank: This is the only finding matching the timeframe and symptom (email slowness starting March 9), and it directly and explicitly rules out the deploy the engineer suspected.

hypotheses.summary: The data cannot determine what actually caused the throttling or its recovery. Two competing explanations remain open: (H1) provider-side rate limiting that resolved on its own, with the later e18d773 deploy (2026-03-10, 'Bump provider SDK') landing inside the recovery window purely by coincidence; or (H2) a pre-existing client-side concurrency/rate-limiting issue that provoked the provider's 429s, which was actually fixed by e18d773 rather than resolving spontaneously. The 429 incident affected 5 of 5 email sends on March 9 across 5 distinct tenants, which is not obviously tenant- or message-specific (weighing toward H1) but does not rule out H2.
hypotheses.why_this_rank: Surfaced per rule 4: this finding is explicitly marked ambiguous with two alternatives the data cannot separate, and the deploy that possibly fixed things (not the one suspected) falls inside the ambiguous window.

ruled_out.claim: The comms-sender deploy c52a0f9 from March 9th (adding an SMS provider seam) caused the email slowness.
ruled_out.why_not: The deploy at 2026-03-09T14:00:00.000Z postdates the onset of the slow-send incident by 5 hours, and 3 of the 6 affected email messages had already been slow before the deploy occurred.

would_resolve: the e18d773 diff — if PR #101 changed connection pooling, concurrency, or retry configuration, H2 gains weight; if it was a version bump with no client-behaviour change, H1 does
provider-side account rate-limit metrics for the incident window
whether other producers on the shared quota saw the same throttling
